skill.name: it-operations
skill.description: Guides IT operations work across infrastructure, monitoring, incident response, automation, backup, recovery, and reliability practices.
skill.summary: IT operations guidance for reliable infrastructure, incidents, monitoring, automation, and recovery.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings come from Markdown runbooks and example scripts for IT operations. Confirmed risks include privileged command execution, credential handling, email or API egress, service persistence, disk formatting, and sensitive access-file changes. Dismissed findings were mainly markdown fences, placeholders, defensive ransomware references, and non-executable prose; no prompt injection attempt was found.

remediation.issue: Destructive storage and privileged host commands appear in copy-paste examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit safety gates, dry-run steps, environment checks, and warnings before mkfs, lvremove, user, service, registry, and firewall operations.

remediation.issue: Credential examples appear in scripts and configuration snippets.
remediation.suggestion: Replace inline credentials and weak defaults with secret manager references and clear rotation guidance.

remediation.issue: The ChatOps health-check flow accepts an arbitrary host target.
remediation.suggestion: Require host allowlists, role checks, audit logging, and approval before running remote Ansible shell modules.

remediation.issue: The Terraform workflow can auto-apply infrastructure changes.
remediation.suggestion: Add manual approvals, plan review, protected environments, and least-privilege cloud credentials before apply.

remediation.issue: Several examples use predictable temporary file paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use secure temporary files, restrictive permissions, cleanup traps, and avoid staging sensitive backups in shared temp directories.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted ChatOps Host Targeting
semantic_findings.description: The health-check command uses Slack command text as the Ansible host target and then runs a shell module. Without an allowlist or authorization check, a ChatOps user could target unintended hosts or groups.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly assigns command text to hostname and passes it to ansible with the shell module. The restart command has a whitelist, but this health-check path does not.

semantic_findings.title: Terraform Auto-Apply Without Manual Approval
semantic_findings.description: The CI workflow configures AWS credentials and runs Terraform apply with auto approval on pushes to main. If branch protection fails, infrastructure changes can be applied without a separate human approval gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow uses AWS secrets and terraform apply -auto-approve in the same job. The risk depends on repository controls, but the pattern is clearly present.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Example Credentials
semantic_findings.description: Several examples include weak or placeholder credentials such as an admin stats password, a backup client password, and a Grafana admin password. Users may copy these into real systems if they are not replaced.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The values are examples or placeholders, not verified live secrets. They are still concrete weak credentials in copy-paste operational configuration.

content.user_title: Manage IT Operations with Reliable Runbooks
content.value_statement: IT teams need consistent guidance for incidents, monitoring, changes, and recovery. This skill provides practical runbooks and frameworks for daily operations.
actual_capabilities: Defines incident severity models, escalation paths, and post-incident review practices.
Provides monitoring, alerting, SLO, and dashboard design guidance.
Includes runbook templates for infrastructure, backups, recovery, and troubleshooting.
Covers automation patterns for shell scripts, Ansible, Terraform, and ChatOps.
Summarizes capacity planning, patch management, and operational metrics.
limitations: Command examples require review before use in production.
It does not replace access controls, approvals, or operator judgment.
Some examples use placeholder endpoints, credentials, and infrastructure names.
It does not execute tasks by itself; execution depends on the host tool and permissions.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Production Services
use_cases.description: Use the incident and monitoring guidance to reduce downtime and improve response quality.

use_cases.title: Plan Backup and Recovery
use_cases.description: Create backup schedules, recovery objectives, and disaster recovery exercises for critical systems.

use_cases.title: Create Incident Runbooks
use_cases.description: Draft clear procedures for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Review Service Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review the health of my service. Cover availability, alerts, logs, capacity, and open operational risks.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Incident Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incident runbook for a critical API outage. Include severity, roles, diagnostics, communication, rollback, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Monitoring and Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monitoring plan for a web application. Include SLIs, SLOs, alert thresholds, dashboards, escalation, and noise reduction.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Change with Rollback
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production change plan for a database migration. Include impact, risk, approvals, validation, rollback, communications, and post-change checks.

output_examples.input: Create a P1 incident response plan for a payment outage.
output_examples.output: A plan with severity criteria, commander role, responder tasks, status updates, customer communication, recovery checks, and review actions.

output_examples.input: Improve our alerting for a noisy backend service.
output_examples.output: An alert tuning proposal with actionable signals, sustained thresholds, routing rules, dashboard links, and review metrics.

output_examples.input: Prepare a disaster recovery exercise for the database platform.
output_examples.output: A tabletop exercise plan with scope, recovery objectives, roles, validation steps, timing, risks, and follow-up items.

best_practices: Review every command example before execution and adapt it to your environment.
Require approvals for changes that modify users, services, storage, or network rules.
Keep runbooks current after incidents, drills, and infrastructure changes.
anti_patterns: Running copied commands against production without dry runs or peer review.
Using placeholder credentials, webhook URLs, or passwords in real systems.
Automating destructive storage, user, or firewall changes without rollback plans.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan and document IT operations work, including monitoring, incidents, changes, automation, backups, and recovery.

faq.question: Can it run infrastructure commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any execution depends on the host tool, user approval, and local permissions.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production operations?
faq.answer: Use it as a planning aid. Production actions still need review, testing, access control, and change approval.

faq.question: Does it include incident management guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers severity levels, responder roles, escalation, communications, runbooks, and post-incident reviews.

faq.question: Does it support backup and disaster recovery planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes recovery objectives, backup patterns, restore testing, disaster recovery sites, and exercise planning.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
